title: Reduce streaming token latency: adaptive token loop, flush cadence, and backpressure
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Streaming token latency (tail and first-token P99) has been a recurring customer pain point for short-response workloads. Previous work improved kernel scheduling and KV cache hits, but we still see spikes caused by flush cadence interactions, the per-request token loop waiting for batching windows, and reactive backpressure causing jitter. This PR implements an adaptive token loop and flush cadence that reduces tail latency while preserving throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive token loop: token emission loop now tracks queue depth and recent flush latency to dynamically shorten per-request wait windows when contention is low, and lengthen them when batching efficiency is needed. 2) Flush cadence smoothing: introduce a leaky-bucket based flush timer to avoid synchronized flush storms across requests; timers jitter is correlated to route-level load. 3) Backpressure prioritization: refine backpressure signals so streaming in-flight small responses are favored for earlier flush when GPU load is uneven (gives short chat responses lower effective latency). 4) Scheduler hint: inject a lightweight hint into kernel scheduler for short sequences to prefer earlier kernel launches when small-batch flush is predicted. 5) KV cache prefetch window tuning: prefetch window reduced for short-response routes to avoid KV-cache misses becoming a tail contributor. Benchmarks: microbench (local perf-canary) shows median token latency unchanged, P95 reduced by ~18%, P99 reduced by ~28% for short-response workloads (avg seq_len < 32). End-to-end streaming tests on dedicated staging (n=3 runs) show 15-22% reduction in first-token latency P99 and ~12% improvement in overall request latency under mixed load. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout (runtime flag streaming.adaptive_token_loop) -> enable on Canary pool for 24h -> 50% rollout on Dedicated -> global rollout if no regressions. Backwards compatibility: all changes are feature-flag guarded and defaults keep current behavior. No API changes. See release notes.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial adaptive loop + tests; flush-cadence smoothing and leaky-bucket timer; scheduler hint and KV prefetch tuning; each commit has unit and integration tests added
patch_highlights: runtime/streaming/token_loop.rs: added adaptive wait window and metrics (emit_wait_suggestion); runtime/streaming/flush_timer.rs: new leaky-bucket flush timer with jitter; runtime/scheduler/kernel_scheduler.rs: accept optional short_sequence hint; runtime/kv_cache/kv_cache.rs: tuned prefetch window for short routes; continuous_batcher: expose queue_depth metric for adaptive loop; tests: added bench harness and regression test for backpressure scenarios

ci_checks: CI pipeline: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), benchmarks (pass). One flaky test in earlier run fixed (streaming_timer_test), rerun passed.
release_notes: Reduce streaming token latency for short-response routes by adaptive token loop, flush cadence smoothing, and backpressure improvements. Feature gated; enable via runtime flag streaming.adaptive_token_loop. Improves P95/P99 for first-token latency in mixed workloads.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for adaptive wait logic, leaky-bucket timer, scheduler hint plumbing, and KV prefetch route override. Integration tests simulate mixed short/long workloads and backpressure. Benchmarks added under tests/benchmarks for perf-canary runs.
follow_up: 1) Observe route-level mismatch counter for 72h post-rollout and tune leaky-bucket params if mismatch > 0.5% of requests. 2) Consider exposing adaptive loop telemetry in Console per-route dashboard. 3) Evaluate kernel hint effectiveness across different GPU topologies.
notes: No customer-facing API changes. Configurable rollout; rolling back is a flag flip. Shiproom: perf team notified; SRE to watch replica-queue metrics.
